# dsh-side-chat
A **side chat** for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI: open the right sidebar from the session header, ad
d the **Side chat** (「侧边会话」) tab, and keep the main conversation untouched — while the side conversa
tion still carries the same agent, the same tools, and **really edits the same workspace files**.

tting the Desktop app before installing into `desktop` (the CLI waits on the profile write lock) and
reopen it afterwards; either way a restart is required. `add` also appends the bundle to the profil
e's `dsh.profile.bundles`; you do not edit the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by hand. Re-running is s
`dsh.profile.bundles`; you do not edit the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by hand. Re-running is safe.

## What it does
- **Native sidebar tab** — lives in the session's right sidebar next to the other tabs; no standalon

e session-header button and no floating overlay.
- **Several at once** — a parent session can hold m
ultiple independent side-chat tabs, each its own ephemeral side session with a numbered chip; open a

nother from the guide card or from a tab's **New side chat** button.
- **Inherits context** — the pa
rent's completed turns plus a snapshot of what the main session is doing right now, taken when that

side chat is created.
- **Inherits the agent** — same working directory, preset composition, tools,

skills, model routing, sandbox mode and approval policy.
- **Really edits files** — write/edit/bash

changes land in the same workspace and the main session sees them.
- **References files with `@`** —
typing `@` in the side-chat composer opens a workspace path menu and inserts the same `@path` menti
on the main composer writes; the pick is text only, so the model reads the file with its normal tool
s. Directory picks keep the menu open to descend, and sent user bubbles show file/folder references

as chips.
- **Isolates the transcript** — side-chat turns never appear in the main conversation, the

session list, or the subagent catalog.
- **Streams the reply** — assistant text, reasoning and tool
calls render token by token from a live event stream while the turn runs; when the transport cannot

stream, the tab falls back to polling.
- **Shows its own usage** — a slim dock under the composer (
the same spot as DSH's main composer dock) shows this side chat's total tokens, cache-hit percentage
, and a small context-occupancy ring + percentage. Hover for the exact uncached-input, cache-read an
d output counts (plus a cache-write count when the provider reports one) and the approximate `~used
/ window` pair. The dock starts hidden until the side chat has a usage sample, and it resets with ea

ch new side session.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
- DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (Desktop profile, Web GUI) — the tested target. This release was verified against
a real `dsh web` process in an isolated DSH home with a fresh `web` profile: the plugin launches, t
he host routes answer (including the SSE route's JSON fallback), and the client bundle is served. Th
e `@file` route added since that run is covered by host-route unit tests rather than a real-process

check.
- No `engines.dsh` and no DSH peer dependency are declared, so DSH does not version-gate inst

allation. That is separate from the tested version: newer DSH releases are untested.
- Web platform

only (`dsh.client.platform: web`); no CLI/TUI surface.
- Node.js `>= 22`; the plugin itself is depen

dency-free ESM with no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports.
- UI copy follows the DSH language setting (Setting
s → General → Language): Chinese and English are built in, and any other language falls back to Engl
ish. Technical details — host error messages, routes, event and tool names — stay in English.
## Known limitations
- Approval prompts are not shown inside the side-chat tab: the side session inherits the parent's ap
proval policy, and if that policy asks a human, the side session waits. Use a non-interactive policy

(for example `danger-full-access`) for side chats that must write files.
- A closed tab cannot be r
estored: reopening the guide card or pressing **New side chat** starts a new side chat, whose agent

is created on the next message.
- P1b, designed but not implemented: model picker, surviving a GUI r

estart, approval rendering in the tab.
- `@` completion depends on the host file-reference provider
and only completes files and folders: `@session` references, `/` commands and skills, attachments an

d drag-and-drop are not part of the side-chat composer yet.
- The inherited context is a snapshot ta
ken when that side chat is created; later main-session turns are not pushed into an existing side ch

at, and each side chat keeps its own snapshot.
- Token streaming rides on a streamable `fetch` respo
nse. If the page transport buffers the response (detected by a missing first frame), the tab falls b
ack to snapshot polling: the running indicator returns and the reply still appears while it grows, a

t poll granularity.
- Each side chat's first request is roughly as large as the parent's next reques

t (it carries the inherited history), so N concurrent side chats multiply that first-request cost.
-
The usage dock is approximate and side-scoped: its token totals and cache-hit percentage cover what
this side chat itself billed — its own requests, including the inherited context its first request
re-sends — and never the parent's earlier requests; its context percentage is absolute for the same
reason, and it omits DSH's projected-token correction, so it can trail the main composer's context b
ar by up to one step. It shows no turns, steps or tok/s, has no click-open dialogs, and cannot follo

w DSH's Performance & usage detailed/compact preference; its content is fixed.
[该节后续省略]
